plan: With a private value of $20, I want to maximize my potential profit. Since this is a second-price sealed bid auction, my optimal strategy is to bid close to, but slightly below my true value. Other rational bidders will likely do the same. Given the random value distribution, I'll bid $19.9 - this leaves a small potential profit margin if I win, and protects against overpaying while still being highly competitive.

In a second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$20, the optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. Since my value is $17, I want to bid high enough to likely win, but not so high that I risk paying more than my value. Other rational bidders will likely do the same. I'll bid slightly below my true value at $16.5 to give myself a good chance of winning while protecting some potential profit margin.

In a single-round sealed bid auction with values between $0-$20, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly less than my true value. Since my value is $13, I want to win without overpaying. Other rational bidders will likely bid similarly. I'll aim to bid around $10-$11 to create a buffer that increases my chances of winning while protecting potential profit margin. This strategy balances winning probability with minimizing potential overpayment.
